title: A Team Member Repairing a Damaged Reputation Needs to Make a Sacrifice
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article maps out how a team member can rebuild a badly damaged reputation, starting with a required first step: owning the mistake and issuing a real apology, whether privately or, for more serious missteps, in a group acknowledgment. It stresses that consistent behavior over time is what actually rebuilds credibility, but singles out visible personal sacrifice as the most powerful accelerant, since it demonstrates commitment through action rather than words. The piece lists concrete examples of sacrifice — taking on unglamorous assignments, onboarding new colleagues, giving up status or perks — and argues the size of the sacrifice is directly proportional to how quickly the team is willing to forgive and move on. It closes by framing sacrifice as sometimes the only thing capable of shifting an already hardened perception.
points: Rebuilding a damaged reputation starts with explicitly owning the mistake and apologizing, privately or, for serious missteps, before the whole group.
Consistency of behavior over time is what actually rebuilds trust, but is described as necessary rather than sufficient on its own.
Visible personal sacrifice — unglamorous assignments, onboarding duties, giving up status or perks — functions as proof of commitment that words alone can't provide.
The size of the sacrifice made is described as directly proportional to how quickly a team is willing to forgive and move forward.
quotes: It takes years to build a solid reputation on a team. But only minutes to destroy it.
Team members serious about reestablishing their credibility must first own the mistake or set of bad actions and issue an apology to the team and the leader.
Consistency in behavior, attitude, and engagement will eventually replace the damaged reputation with a new and better one if the team member can avoid any new mishaps.
Repairing a damaged reputation nearly always benefits from a sacrifice to prove how serious the offender is in making a fresh start.

Sacrifice communicates a real shift in priorities, demonstrating with actions, not words, that the team’s success and trust are of the highest importance. The greater the sacrifice, the more likely the team will forgive and forget over time.
